new_statements.quote: The Katu word has a main syllable which can be preceded by one, two or three presyllables. The word can be symbolised as CV3/CV2/CV1/MS. CV3 and CV2 are always affixes, whereas CV1 is rarely an affix. Presyllables are always unstressed. The main syllable MS can be symbolised as CV±C or CCV.

new_statements.rule_in_words: Katu words are sesquisyllabic: a main syllable (CV±C or CCV) optionally preceded by up to three presyllables (CV3/CV2/CV1), and the presyllables are always unstressed, so word prominence falls on the final, main syllable. Stress is therefore fixed on the last (main) syllable; it is a phonotactic/structural property rather than a contrastive one.
new_statements.exceptions: None stated; the same statement is given for all three dialects the dictionary covers (An-Diem, Phu-Hoa, High Katu).
new_statements.domain_note: Phonological word (dictionary entries, i.e. citation forms); nothing said about phrase-level prominence. The statement covers the Katu of Quang Nam (Low Katu An-Diem and Phu-Hoa, High Katu); its application to Phuong rests on Glottolog's identification High Katu = Phuong [phg].
new_statements.identity_note: No description written for "Phuong" as such exists. Glottolog 5.3 keeps phuo1238/phg as a language (Katuic > Katu; alt names Huu River Vân Kiêu, Phuang, Phuong Catang; AES 6a Vigorous, ethnic group Cơ Tu) but its entire bibliography for phg is Costello's Katu dictionary (1991) and Katu vocabulary (1971), tagged in hh.bib `lgcode = {Eastern Katu [ktv], High Katu = Phuong [phg]}`; Wikipedia likewise glosses Phuong as "High Katu", and Glottolog's Eastern Katu page (east1236, ktv) now also lists Phuong/Phuang/Phuong Katu/High Katu among its names. The quoted statement is Costello's for Katu as a whole: her 1991 dictionary covers two Low Katu dialects (An-Diem, Phu-Hoa) and one High Katu dialect (marked hk, ~75% vocabulary correspondence with An-Diem), all in Quang Nam west of Da Nang (page image). The equation High Katu = Phuong is Glottolog's/Wikipedia's, not Costello's; Glottolog's phg coordinates (16.21N 107.47E) fall in Thua Thien-Hue (Nam Dong), where SIL's Phuong is located. Catalog entry should be coded for Katu (east1236/ktv incl. High Katu) with phuo1238 as Glottolog-identified same variety.
